pr.body:
…tory

closes #33831

This is the Keycloak main part for solving the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 and adding the related changes in the authz-client on the Keycloak side, which can then be later synced to the keycloak-client repository. 

In the end, I am using approach (2) from https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 with adding the method `order()` to `CryptoProvider`, which allows to have multiple instances of `CryptoProvider` on classpath (Keycloak testsuite still uses the `DefaultCryptoProvider` as before this PR).

raw_findings.body: Existing implementations no longer compile, and pre-compiled implementations fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during service loading.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Binary/source incompatibility for external CryptoProvider implementations.
raw_findings.impact: Existing implementations no longer compile, and pre-compiled implementations fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during service loading.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new method was added to a published SPI interface without a default implementation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the method with a default implementation, e.g. `default int order() { return 200; }`, so existing implementors keep working and only providers needing a different priority override it.
raw_findings.title: New abstract `order()` on public CryptoProvider SPI breaks existing implementations
raw_findings.trigger: Any third-party or downstream module that already implements `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` (a published interface in keycloak-common) is recompiled or loaded against the new keycloak-common jar.

raw_findings.body: Instead of failing fast with an explicit IllegalStateException, `detectProvider` silently returns whichever equal-order provider ServiceLoader happened to enumerate first, so a deployment may run in non-FIPS mode (or vice versa) with only a debug-level log line.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent, non-deterministic crypto provider selection where the previous behavior was an explicit configuration error.
raw_findings.impact: Instead of failing fast with an explicit IllegalStateException, `detectProvider` silently returns whichever equal-order provider ServiceLoader happened to enumerate first, so a deployment may run in non-FIPS mode (or vice versa) with only a debug-level log line.
raw_findings.root_cause: The ambiguity check was replaced with an ordering heuristic even though all shipped providers were given the identical order value 200.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a hard failure for ambiguity: after sorting, throw IllegalStateException when `foundProviders.size() > 1` and the first two entries have the same `order()` value.
raw_findings.title: Removal of the multiple-provider guard makes equal-order providers resolve non-deterministically
raw_findings.trigger: A misconfigured classpath containing two providers that this patch gives the same order value, e.g. `DefaultCryptoProvider` (order 200) and `FIPS1402Provider` (order 200), both discovered by the ServiceLoader.

raw_findings.body: Two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to on every signature conversion; their results are discarded, wasting allocations and misleading readers into thinking the encoding happens here rather than in the following `writeDerSeq(...)` call.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unused side-effect-free code obscures intent and adds per-call allocations.
raw_findings.impact: Two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to on every signature conversion; their results are discarded, wasting allocations and misleading readers into thinking the encoding happens here rather than in the following `writeDerSeq(...)` call.
raw_findings.root_cause: Leftover scaffolding statements were kept after the encoding was moved into the `writeDerSeq` call.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete both statements; the DER sequence is already built by the `writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))` expression below.
raw_findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
raw_findings.trigger: Every call to `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, e.g. when the authz-client verifies an ES256 signature.

raw_findings.body: The assertion compares the decoder output with itself after a full round trip through the new encoder and decoder, so a mutually consistent but non-DER-compliant encoding passes the test while real Keycloak servers would reject the signature.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test cannot detect an incorrect DER encoding produced by the newly added ASN1Encoder.
raw_findings.impact: The assertion compares the decoder output with itself after a full round trip through the new encoder and decoder, so a mutually consistent but non-DER-compliant encoding passes the test while real Keycloak servers would reject the signature.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test asserts only encoder/decoder symmetry instead of comparing against a trusted DER implementation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an independent oracle to `test(...)`: verify `asn1Des` with `Signature.getInstance(...).initVerify(keyPair.getPublic())`/`verify(asn1Des)` (and/or assert `asn1Des` equals the JDK-produced `sign`) so the encoder output is validated against the JDK DER parser.
raw_findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest only checks self round-trip, never validates the produced DER
raw_findings.trigger: Run the new test against an `ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder` pair that encodes and decodes with a matching but non-standard (e.g. wrong tag or length) representation.

raw_findings.body: The 384/512 cases only ever see 32-byte r/s values zero-padded to 48/66 bytes, so the realistic P-384/P-521 signature sizes and the `qLength < bytes.length` truncation path of `integerToBytes` are never exercised for those algorithms; a length-handling bug for real ES384/ES512 signatures would go undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Tests pass without covering the signature lengths they claim to cover.
raw_findings.impact: The 384/512 cases only ever see 32-byte r/s values zero-padded to 48/66 bytes, so the realistic P-384/P-521 signature sizes and the `qLength < bytes.length` truncation path of `integerToBytes` are never exercised for those algorithms; a length-handling bug for real ES384/ES512 signatures would go undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: A single default-curve key pair is reused for all three ECDSA algorithms.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate a key pair per algorithm using `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` initialized with `new ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"/"secp384r1"/"secp521r1")` matching the tested ECDSAAlgorithm.
raw_findings.title: ES384/ES512 test cases use a default P-256 key instead of matching curves
raw_findings.trigger: `testES384` and `testES512` run with the shared key pair generated here, which on standard JDKs defaults to secp256r1 (256-bit).

raw_findings.body: The already-formatted message is treated as a printf format string (any '%' in a provider class name would raise an IllegalFormatException) and the emitted text ends with a dangling ", " separator.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed log output and an avoidable formatting failure path in a diagnostic code path.
raw_findings.impact: The already-formatted message is treated as a printf format string (any '%' in a provider class name would raise an IllegalFormatException) and the emitted text ends with a dangling ", " separator.
raw_findings.root_cause: A non-constant, already-formatted string is passed to a printf-style logging method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `logger.debug(...)` with the pre-built message and drop the trailing separator, e.g. join the ignored provider names with `", "` instead of appending it after each entry.
raw_findings.title: Dynamically built message passed as a format string to logger.debugf
raw_findings.trigger: Debug logging enabled with more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath.

raw_findings.body: An unreferenced dependency is pulled into the module's test classpath, adding maintenance/resolution surface and potentially failing dependency-analysis checks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unused build dependency introduced by the patch.
raw_findings.impact: An unreferenced dependency is pulled into the module's test classpath, adding maintenance/resolution surface and potentially failing dependency-analysis checks.
raw_findings.root_cause: Test dependency block was copied wholesale without the corresponding test usage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the hamcrest dependency, or use `org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat` in the new test so the dependency is actually needed.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `logger.debug(...)` with the pre-built message and drop the trailing separator, e.g. join the ignored provider names with `", "` instead of appending it after each entry.
validated_findings.title: Dynamically built message passed as a format string to logger.debugf
validated_findings.trigger: Debug logging enabled with more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 69 shows logger.debugf(builder.toString()) where builder contains user-controlled class names. If a class name contains '%', IllegalFormatException is thrown. Also trailing ', ' separator is present.
